fields.name: Let me give you a piece of free advice.
fields.definition: Flocks with a neighborhood radius of 0 don't FLOCK, per se (in the creature-creature interaction kind of way), but they are much cheaper. The best thing is to have a non-zero radius for small flocks, and a zero radius for large flocks (or for 'flow-flocks', ones with sources and sinks that are intended to create a steady flow of something). Note also that for flocks with a 0 neighborhood radius, the parameters for avoidance, alignment, position and perception angle are ignored entirely.

fields.name: neighborhood radius:world units#distance within which one boid is affected by another
avoidance radius:world units#distance that a boid tries to maintain from another
forward scale:[0..1]#weight given to boid's desire to fly straight ahead
alignment scale:[0..1]#weight given to boid's desire to align itself with neighboring boids
avoidance scale:[0..1]#weight given to boid's desire to avoid collisions with other boids, when within the avoidance radius
leveling force scale:[0..1]#weight given to boids desire to fly level
sink scale:[0..1]#weight given to boid's desire to fly towards its sinks
perception angle:degrees#angle-from-forward within which one boid can perceive and react to another
average throttle:[0..1]#throttle at which boids will naturally fly
position scale:[0..1]#weight given to boid's desire to be near flock center
position min radius:wus#distance to flock center beyond which an attracting force is applied
position max radius:wus#distance to flock center at which the maximum attracting force is applied
movement weight threshold#The threshold of accumulated weight over which movement occurs
danger radius:wus#distance within which boids will avoid a dangerous object (e.g. the player)
danger scale#weight given to boid's desire to avoid danger
